title: Soveraeign Authority Grant (PROPOSED, decisions/0061)
description: The AuthorityGrant object SPEC.md declares at its Authority section, compiled into a machine contract. A grant is typed, scoped, budgeted, time-bounded, and revocable; an authority check evaluates type, capability, scope, budget, time, and revocation at the attempted transition (SPEC.md, PROD-I-5). A grant is the only thing that carries authority: a lease says who is on the hook, a receipt says what happened, and neither confers anything. Semantic constraints a schema cannot express - a path outside scope, an exhausted budget, a witness that was inside the build - are checked by scripts/sovkernel/authority.py and named in the fixtures that defeat them.

issuer_id.description: Who issued it. JUDGEMENT authority may be issued by the owner and by nobody else; the evaluator enforces that, not this schema.

actor_id.description: Who may exercise it. A profile name such as `sov` names any participant loaded under that profile, which is what makes one grant serve both a human-driven session and a launched agent.

capabilities.description: The named transitions this grant covers. `*` is not admitted: a grant that covers everything is not scoped, and PROD-I-5 requires scope.

effect_ceiling.description: The furthest effect class this grant reaches. A request declaring a heavier class than the ceiling is refused even inside scope.

preconditions_by_capability.description: Additional preconditions keyed by a capability this grant carries. Capability-key syntax is checked by the authority evaluator/test corpus because the repository's bounded JSON Schema profile does not implement propertyNames. This keeps one scoped grant from forcing a later transition's evidence onto an earlier one; for example repository.commit may freeze a candidate before repository.land requires independent observation of that frozen subject.

valid_until.description: A grant with no end is not a grant. An expiry that has to be renewed is what keeps a standing authorization a decision rather than a habit.

scope.description: Where the grant reaches in the repository. Prefixes, matched against the paths a request declares it changed. An exclusion always beats an inclusion, so a narrower rule cannot be widened by adding a broader one.

branches.description: Which branches the grant may land on. Absent means the working branch only.

budget.description: What exercising the grant may spend, in one named unit. A null ceiling is uncapped and is admitted only for a RECORD_LOCAL grant, because an uncapped grant that can consume resources is the case PROD-I-5 names as refusing visibly.

preconditions.description: What must already be true and evidenced before the grant may be exercised. Each named check must be present in the request's evidence and reading PASS; a check that is absent is absent, never satisfied.
